unnamed_clusters.rule: An unnamed cluster is a set of wallets found from the chain's own transfers by a written rule. No public source names them, so they have no name here, and the rule says nothing about who holds them. The redemption route (`issuer_route`) has three kinds of wallet. The hub is the wallet a chain's mints go to. Path wallets are on the fixed path from the hub into burns. Collection wallets take money from many senders, send every outgoing transfer to the hub, and hold almost no balance. A wallet that passes money through from a single sender stays unlabeled, as does any other wallet with flows into the route, however large the flows. A contract on the path may have a verified name on the chain, but that name doesn't say who runs it, so the label stays unnamed. Published data gives a count of these wallets by chain and category, with this rule. Their addresses are only in `labels/labels.csv` in this repository.

source_types.meaning: A block explorer shows this name on the address
source_types.how_to_check: Open the link and read the name at the top of the address page

source_types.meaning: The documentation or app of the project that runs the contract lists it under this name
source_types.how_to_check: Open the link and find the name, with its address beside it

source_types.meaning: A company's own documentation names the address as its own
source_types.how_to_check: Open the link and find the name, with its address beside it

source_types.meaning: The named organization said so in an announcement or other statement
source_types.how_to_check: Open the link and find the name and address in the statement

source_types.meaning: A named research publisher ties the name to the address
source_types.how_to_check: Open the link and find the name and address. Publishers may shorten an address, as in `0x4c2c…00b8`

source_types.meaning: The chain itself records it, such as a verified contract name and its creator
source_types.how_to_check: Open the link and read the contract details

source_types.meaning: No source names it. It is an unnamed cluster, found by a written rule applied to the chain's own data
source_types.how_to_check: Read the rule at the link. The dataset publishes no address for an unnamed cluster, so apply it to the addresses in `labels/labels.csv` in this repository

source_legend.reading_a_label: a named label always has a web source you can open. A `derived_rule` label never has a name, because it describes what a wallet does, not who holds it. `confidence` is `medium` when the source leaves a gap, such as a vault page that shows no curator, or research that prints only a shortened address. Vault names come from the vault's creator, not from any company the name may suggest, so a name alone doesn't say who runs a vault. The 0x Settler labels rest on the verified contract name and on the creator the chain records for it, `deployer.zeroexprotocol.eth`. Tell us if a source no longer supports a label.
